antipatterns.definition: The change satisfies the checks it was optimized against and breaks untested but intended behavior.
antipatterns.detector: A held-out oracle disagrees with the optimized oracle.
antipatterns.name: Oracle Overfit

antipatterns.definition: The gate is weakened, narrowed or deleted so that it passes.
antipatterns.detector: The diff touches the check and the check's strictness decreased.
antipatterns.name: Oracle Laundering

antipatterns.definition: Delivered work covers less than was asked and the report does not say so.
antipatterns.detector: A requested acceptance item has neither an artifact nor an explicit deferral.
antipatterns.name: Silent Scope Narrowing

antipatterns.definition: Done is declared with no verification step executed.
antipatterns.detector: No gate invocation appears in the trace.
antipatterns.name: Unverified Completion

antipatterns.definition: The run ends before producing the information needed to close the task.
antipatterns.detector: Handoff conditions are unmet at exit.
antipatterns.name: Premature Termination

antipatterns.definition: Equivalent actions repeat without changing observable state.
antipatterns.detector: Repeated action/observation pairs above a threshold.
antipatterns.name: No-Progress Oscillation

antipatterns.definition: A cited file, symbol or source does not exist, or does not support the claim made of it.
antipatterns.detector: The reference resolver fails, or the resolved target contradicts the claim.
antipatterns.name: Confabulated Reference

antipatterns.definition: The measuring instrument, not the system, explains the score.
antipatterns.detector: A human re-screen of the items changes the ranking.
antipatterns.name: Benchmark Validity Drift

antipatterns.definition: A sweep is attempted as one atomic change at a scale where it cannot land.
antipatterns.detector: The change cannot pass presubmit as a single unit.
antipatterns.name: Atomicity Overreach

axes.name: Workload shape
axes.question: What is the job, and what artifact counts as done?

axes.name: Orchestration topology
axes.question: How is the work arranged across steps, agents and turns?
axes.values: single interactive loop; fixed staged pipeline; fan-out/fan-in; tree search; human-in-the-loop

axes.name: Verification strategy
axes.question: What evidence closes the loop?
axes.values: executable oracle; derived/pinned oracle; relational (metamorphic) oracle; held-out oracle; independent judge; citation resolution; none

axes.name: Failure mode
axes.question: How does it degrade into a plausible wrong answer?

conflations.claim: Multi-agent (or fan-out, or pipeline) is a workload pattern.
conflations.counterexample: wp.mechanical-sweep runs as a single scripted pass and as a per-shard fan-out; goal, done-artifact, oracle and dominant failure mode (ap.atomicity-overreach) are identical in both. Agentless solves the issue-resolution shape with a fixed localize/repair/validate pipeline rather than an agent loop.

conflations.claim: If it has no test, it is not real engineering work.
conflations.counterexample: wp.comprehension-report has no executable oracle by construction; its verification strategy is citation resolution. A fully test-green wp.issue-to-patch result can still be wrong: patches passing the available tests can overfit them and break untested desired functionality. Test-green is neither necessary nor sufficient.

conflations.claim: Bisect (or localization, or review) is a workload.
conflations.counterexample: sp.history-bisection appears inside wp.issue-to-patch, inside wp.perf-under-invariant (the git bisect manual names benchmark movement as a target property) and inside wp.env-remediation. A move reusable across shapes cannot itself be the shape.

conflations.claim: The Workflow Patterns catalogue already names these workloads.
conflations.counterexample: Workflow patterns are control-flow constructs for comparing workflow management systems. Parallel Split describes a mechanical code sweep and a document-translation pipeline identically, because it is silent about what the work is and what makes it correct. It is the right vocabulary for ax.orchestration-topology and the wrong one for ax.workload-shape.

wp.behavior-preserving-restructure asserts observable behavior is unchanged; wp.issue-to-patch asserts exactly one observable behavior changed. A change doing both has no single passing oracle: the pin fails at the fixed site and the repair witness cannot distinguish fixed from moved. The expand/migrate/contract discipline exists because the phases stay separate and the code is never broken between them.

conflations.claim: A red build is a bug in the program.
conflations.counterexample: SWE-bench Verified screening found environments that were difficult to set up reliably, causing unit tests to fail regardless of the solution, alongside over-specific tests and under-specified issues. Those are wp.env-remediation and ap.benchmark-validity-drift, not defects in the program under test; routing them to wp.issue-to-patch produces edits to correct code.

demotion_evidence: Retire an element when annotators cannot separate it from a neighbour without inventing a criterion absent from this artifact. Demote the whole proposal if a survey published after 2026-08-10 supplies an equivalent axis split with broader evidence; then borrow it and keep only the new-synthesis entries that survive.
id_mapping_note: Canonical shipped detectors use wp.* for workload patterns and sp.* for reusable moves; this proposal corpus is source evidence and must be adapted explicitly.
invalidating_assumptions: The four axes are assumed independent. If workload shape predicts orchestration topology strongly enough across real trajectories that topology carries no additional information, ax.orchestration-topology is a derived attribute and the four-axis claim is wrong.

The four new-synthesis elements (wp.env-remediation, wp.comprehension-report, sp.blast-radius-scoping, sp.citation-binding) are assumed genuinely unnamed. They rest on a corpus verified at abstract granularity by one worker on one day; a full-text sweep, or literature outside the surveyed streams, could show any of them is a rename.

Sources are assumed to say what their abstracts say. Verification did not reach full text (WebFetch refused at this host's capability floor). Any attribution the full paper contradicts invalidates that row of the evidence table.

mechanisms.definition: Run untrusted code and observe its effects.
mechanisms.name: Execution sandbox

mechanisms.definition: Select and run checks, reporting per-check status.
mechanisms.name: Test runner

mechanisms.definition: Addressable revisions with checkout and diff.
mechanisms.name: Version-control history

mechanisms.definition: Apply and revert a diff safely.
mechanisms.name: Patch applier

mechanisms.definition: Exclusive claim over a declared file region.
mechanisms.name: Write lease

mechanisms.definition: Bounded, observable step and token accounting.
mechanisms.name: Step budget

mechanisms.definition: A second model or human that never sees author-side rationale.
mechanisms.name: Judge channel

mechanisms.definition: Resolve a citation to its target and compare.
mechanisms.name: Reference resolver

patterns.definition: Turn a reported defect into a change that alters exactly the reported behavior.
patterns.exclude_when: No prior defect claim; or the check itself is the deliverable.
patterns.include_when: A defect claim exists and the done-artifact is a diff.
patterns.name: Issue-to-Patch Repair

patterns.definition: Add an externally visible capability described in prose while preserving existing behavior.
patterns.exclude_when: The capability exists but misbehaves (that is wp.issue-to-patch).
patterns.include_when: The described capability does not exist yet.
patterns.name: Specification-to-Feature Construction

patterns.definition: Change internal structure while asserting that observable behavior is unchanged.
patterns.exclude_when: Any observable output is intended to change.
patterns.include_when: The success oracle is that nothing observable changed.
patterns.name: Behavior-Preserving Restructuring

patterns.definition: Apply one verified rewrite rule across many sites that cannot land as a single atomic change.
patterns.exclude_when: One site, or per-site human judgment is required.
patterns.include_when: The rule is decidable per site and site count dominates the cost.
patterns.name: Mechanical Fleet-Wide Sweep

patterns.definition: Change an interface incompatibly while its consumers keep working throughout.
patterns.exclude_when: No consumer outside the change's own footprint.
patterns.include_when: Consumers exist and cannot be updated atomically.
patterns.name: Interface Migration Under Live Consumers

patterns.definition: Restore a runnable build/test environment when the defect is in the environment, not the program.
patterns.exclude_when: Program logic is wrong under one toolchain (that is wp.issue-to-patch).
patterns.include_when: The failure reproduces with no program logic being wrong.
patterns.name: Environment and Dependency Remediation

patterns.definition: Produce the check itself: tests, properties, metamorphic relations or fixtures.
patterns.exclude_when: A failing test written as a step toward a fix (that is sp.reproduce-first).
patterns.include_when: The delivered artifact is the check.
patterns.name: Oracle Construction

patterns.definition: Answer a question about a system; the deliverable is a cited explanation, not a diff.
patterns.exclude_when: A diff is required for success.
patterns.include_when: No source mutation is required for success.
patterns.name: Comprehension and Explanation Report

patterns.definition: Decide what happens to an item - route, assign, dedupe, defer - without changing the program.
patterns.exclude_when: The deliverable is the fix itself.
patterns.include_when: The deliverable is a decision about an item.
patterns.name: Triage and Routing

patterns.definition: Judge a proposed change and its evidence, returning a verdict and findings.
patterns.exclude_when: The same actor also authored the change.
patterns.include_when: Input is a candidate change plus its evidence.
patterns.name: Change Adjudication

patterns.definition: Move a measured quantity while a behavior pin holds.
patterns.exclude_when: Accepted on a plausibility argument with no measurement.
patterns.include_when: Success requires a measurement against a named baseline.
patterns.name: Performance Optimization Under Invariant

promotion_evidence: Two independent annotators classify a sample of this repository's trajectories using only the published inclusion/exclusion criteria and reach substantial agreement on ax.workload-shape without consulting each other, AND at least one downstream consumer (dispatch classifier, report schema or issue template) reads the wp.*/sp.* identifiers instead of re-deriving its own names.

provenance_labels.adapted: Concept is cited; the name, boundary or scope is ours.
provenance_labels.borrowed: Name and concept both come from a cited source and are adopted unchanged.
provenance_labels.new-synthesis: No cited source names this element; the citation supports only its ingredients.

subpatterns.definition: Build a deterministic check that fails now and would pass on success, before editing.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The claim is about structure or prose, not behavior.
subpatterns.include_when: A behavioral claim can be executed.
subpatterns.name: Reproduce First

subpatterns.definition: Shrink a failing input while the failure is preserved, down to a 1-minimal remainder.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The failure depends on unreproducible external state.
subpatterns.include_when: The failure is input-triggered and re-runnable.
subpatterns.name: Input Minimization

subpatterns.definition: Binary-search revisions for the first commit at which a monotone property flips.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The property is not decidable at an arbitrary revision.
subpatterns.include_when: History is navigable and the property is testable per revision.
subpatterns.name: History Bisection

subpatterns.definition: Rank suspect code by coverage difference between passing and failing runs.
subpatterns.exclude_when: No executable suite exists.
subpatterns.include_when: A suite with both passing and failing runs exists.
subpatterns.name: Spectrum Localization

subpatterns.definition: Narrow file to class/function to edit site in fixed stages, with no interactive loop.
subpatterns.exclude_when: Localization needs feedback from execution.
subpatterns.include_when: The repo is large and each stage is cheap.
subpatterns.name: Hierarchical Localization

subpatterns.definition: Retrieve context through program structure (AST/symbols) rather than text similarity.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The artifact is prose or opaque data.
subpatterns.include_when: A parseable program representation is available.
subpatterns.name: Structured Code Search

subpatterns.definition: Look for existing in-repo code that already implements the change before writing new code.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The change is genuinely novel to the repository.
subpatterns.include_when: The change plausibly resembles code already present.
subpatterns.name: Graft Search

subpatterns.definition: Add the new interface, move consumers, then delete the old one - never broken in between.
subpatterns.exclude_when: A single atomic change is already safe.
subpatterns.include_when: Consumers cannot be moved atomically.
subpatterns.name: Expand, Migrate, Contract

subpatterns.definition: Put a facade in front of the old path, redirect call sites incrementally, then remove the old path.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The old component can be switched off at once.
subpatterns.include_when: The old component must keep serving during replacement.
subpatterns.name: Facade and Drain

subpatterns.definition: Validate the rewrite rule on a small sample, then apply and verify shard by shard.
subpatterns.exclude_when: Sites need individual judgment.
subpatterns.include_when: The rule is mechanical and the sites are many.
subpatterns.name: Rule Then Sweep

subpatterns.definition: Capture current observable behavior as a check before changing anything.
subpatterns.exclude_when: Current behavior is the defect.
subpatterns.include_when: Current behavior is trusted and re-observable.
subpatterns.name: Behavior Pinning

subpatterns.definition: Assert a relation between outputs of related inputs when no expected output is known.
subpatterns.exclude_when: A concrete expected output is available.
subpatterns.include_when: Expected output is unavailable but a relation is known.
subpatterns.name: Metamorphic Relation

subpatterns.definition: Sample many candidates and keep those surviving an executable filter or cross-agreement.
subpatterns.exclude_when: Each candidate is expensive or unverifiable.
subpatterns.include_when: Candidates are cheap and a filter is executable.
subpatterns.name: Generate and Filter

subpatterns.definition: Run, read the actual observation, patch, repeat under an explicit step budget.
subpatterns.exclude_when: Feedback is absent, delayed, or systematically misleading.
subpatterns.include_when: Execution feedback is available and cheap.
subpatterns.name: Execute, Observe, Repair

subpatterns.definition: Carry a written failure summary into the next attempt instead of re-sampling blind.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The failure signal cannot be attributed to a step.
subpatterns.include_when: Attempts are repeatable and failures are describable.
subpatterns.name: Verbal Retrospective

subpatterns.definition: A verifier that did not author the change judges it, with author-side rationale withheld.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The available check is a total decidable oracle.
subpatterns.include_when: The change's correctness is contestable.
subpatterns.name: Independent Adjudication

subpatterns.definition: Reserve a check that the producing step never saw and never optimized against.
subpatterns.exclude_when: Every available check must guide production.
subpatterns.include_when: A check can be withheld without blocking production.
subpatterns.name: Held-Out Oracle

subpatterns.definition: Change the tools and affordances the agent acts through, not the prompt or the model.
subpatterns.exclude_when: Failures trace to missing knowledge.
subpatterns.include_when: Failures trace to action/observation format.
subpatterns.name: Interface Shaping

subpatterns.definition: Declare the write footprint before editing so concurrent work provably cannot collide.
subpatterns.exclude_when: A single serialized writer.
subpatterns.include_when: More than one worker can write the tree.
subpatterns.name: Blast-Radius Scoping

subpatterns.definition: Hand control to a human at a named decision boundary, not at a step-count limit.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The decision is cheap and reversible.
subpatterns.include_when: The decision's cost is asymmetric and its outcome uncertain.
subpatterns.name: Escalation Checkpoint

subpatterns.definition: Bind every assertion to a resolvable pointer that is checked apart from the assertion.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The deliverable is executable and self-checking.
subpatterns.include_when: The deliverable is prose or a report.
subpatterns.name: Citation Binding

subpatterns.definition: Spend a bounded budget in explicit explore mode before committing to one option.
subpatterns.exclude_when: The next step is already known (accelerate mode).
subpatterns.include_when: The approach is genuinely unknown.
subpatterns.name: Budgeted Exploration

verification_method: Title, authors, venue, year and identifier of each source checked on 2026-08-10 against indexed publisher/preprint metadata and abstract text. Direct page fetch was unavailable (WebFetch refused at the host capability floor), so verification granularity is metadata and abstract, not full text.
witnessed_envelope: The cited corpus as of 2026-08-10. A defensible vocabulary proposal, not a claim of field-wide consensus and not a maintained fak contract.
